references.text: God calls Bezalel and Oholiab by name and fills them with His Spirit, wisdom, and understanding to carry out the work of the sanctuary. This is the original appointment that Exodus 36:1 refers back to.

Moses announces to the Israelites that the Lord has called Bezalel and Oholiab and given them wisdom, understanding, and knowledge for all kinds of work. This is the immediate context before the execution in chapter 36.
God gives wisdom to craftsmen to make Aaron's priestly garments. The same principle of God-given wisdom for holy work.
Solomon asks God for wisdom and understanding, and God grants it to him. It shows the pattern where God gives special wisdom for specific tasks.
Hiram from Tyre was filled with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge to carry out all bronze work for the temple. A parallel to Bezalel's God-given abilities.
God teaches the farmer the right way to work. It shows that practical wisdom and skill come from the Lord.
The Lord gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding. The fundamental principle that all true wisdom comes from God.
If anyone lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach. A New Testament parallel about God as the source of wisdom.
The Holy Spirit gives different gifts to various people for service in the church. A New Testament parallel to how God equips people with special abilities for holy service.
Confirmation that the work was completed exactly according to God's command, which begins in 36:1 and concludes with Moses' blessing here.
The connection between God's gift of wisdom to the chosen ones (36:1) and the original call to those who have wisdom in their hearts (35:10).
God's promise to give wisdom to Bezalel and Oholiab (31:6), which was fulfilled when they began the work in 36:1.
Complementary aspects of the sanctuary work: God's gift of wisdom to the craftsmen (36:1) and the people's voluntary offerings (35:29).
Complementary descriptions of the sanctuary work: those with wisdom who carry it out (36:1) and those who are willing to give gifts (35:21).
